rem-sine-period-arc-length-integrand-is-.exact_statement: For nondegenerate modulus $0<k<1$, the complete elliptic integral of the second kind $E(k)=\int_0^{\pi/2}\sqrt{1-k^2\sin^2\theta}\,d\theta$ cannot be evaluated in terms of elementary functions.
rem-sine-period-arc-length-integrand-is-.local_proof_attempt: The preceding example reduces the sine-period arc length to the case $k=1/\sqrt2$. A local proof of non-elementarity would require Liouville's theorem on elementary antiderivatives or equivalent differential-algebra machinery, none of which is available in the declared prerequisite closure and none of which can be built as a small analysis lemma.
rem-sine-period-arc-length-integrand-is-.necessity: The page design explicitly requires the distinction between an exact elliptic-integral value and an elementary antiderivative; separating it into a recorded-not-proved remark keeps the computed length proved locally without pretending to develop differential algebra.
